item.title: Syngenta’s $5 Billion Hong Kong IPO Is Said to Face Fresh Delays
item.description: Syngenta Group’s planned $5 billion Hong Kong initial public offering is facing delays as the seed and pesticide company waits for better conditions in the agriculture sector, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Asian Gas Prices Rise to Highest Since March on Mideast Tensions
item.description: Asian liquefied natural gas prices rose to the highest since late March as fresh hostilities in the Middle East deepened concerns that shipping through the key Strait of Hormuz will remain disrupted for longer.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama Leaves Open Possibility of GPIF Domestic Shift
item.description: Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama reiterated that she will pursue measures to encourage the Government Pension Investment Fund to invest more in domestic financial assets, while stressing she has no authority to step into the fund’s investment decisions.

item.title: Japan’s Robot Makers Join Nvidia’s Physical AI Cosmos Coalition
item.description: Nvidia Corp. and four of Japan’s leading industrial automation companies said they will expand their collaboration on robot development, bolstering Jensen Huang’s push into AI-enabled hardware.

item.title: China Seeks to Curb New Bond Sales by LGFVs With Increased Debt
item.description: A major Chinese bond regulator is taking fresh steps to curb debt sales by the nation’s municipal borrowers, according to people familiar with the matter, adding pressure on weaker issuers looking to refinance notes.

item.title: Nvidia’s Huang Courts Japanese Suppliers With Kanda Pork Skewers
item.description: On Wednesday night, Jensen Huang was in Tokyo’s central Kanda district courting the little-known Japanese suppliers that underpin the AI supply chain.

item.title: Wheat Holds Near Two-Month High After Black Sea Attacks
item.description: Wheat futures held gains after jumping 5% on Wednesday, as Ukrainian and Russian strikes in the Black Sea threatened a key export route for the warring countries.

item.title: Hyundai to Buy SoftBank’s Boston Dynamics Stake in Robot Push
item.description: Hyundai Motor Co. and its affiliates are moving to acquire SoftBank Group Corp.’s remaining stake in the automaker’s Boston Dynamics unit, as the Seoul-based company accelerates commercialization of its Atlas humanoid robot.

item.title: Adani Flagship Draws Mutual Fund Interest as Governance Risks Recede
item.description: Local mutual funds bought Adani Enterprises shares worth 46.60 billion rupees last month.

item.title: Palm Beach Strikes Down Data Center Plan After Local Backlash
item.description: Palm Beach County commissioners rejected a proposal late Wednesday to build a digital infrastructure hub to house AI data centers and warehouses, voting in line with the ardent opposition from local residents.

item.title: Pound Index Hits One-Year High on Mahmood for Chancellor Reports
item.description: A measure of sterling’s strength rose to its highest level in a year on Wednesday following reports that incoming UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will name Shabana Mahmood as his Chancellor of the Exchequer.

item.title: EU, India Move to Expand Ties Beyond Landmark Free Trade Deal
item.description: The European Union and India agreed to start formal talks on New Delhi’s participation in the bloc’s flagship Horizon research program, broadening ties beyond a landmark free trade agreement that’s expected to come into force next year.

item.title: India Raises Export Levies on Diesel and Jet Fuel
item.description: India increased taxes on exports of ‌diesel and aviation turbine fuel as the collapse of the US-Iran interim peace deal and renewed hostilities have choked oil flows again tightening global fuel markets.

item.title: Australia Inflation Expectations Fall to Lowest Since January
item.description: Australia’s expected inflation rate fell to 4.7% in July, the lowest level since January 2026, according to a survey released by the Melbourne Institute.

item.title: Modi Pushes to Cut Import Reliance to Shield India From Shocks
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is taking steps to reduce key imports into the economy in order to protect supply chains and ease pressure on the currency as geopolitical risks escalate.

item.title: Korea Raises Rates for First Time Since 2023 on Chip-Led Boom
item.description: South Korea’s central bank raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years and flagged the possibility of further increases as an artificial intelligence-driven chip boom helps fuel sticky inflation and faster-than-expected economic growth.

item.title: Japan PE Fund Seeks $1.9 Billion Economic-Security Investments
item.description: Advantage Partners LLC plans to invest in big domestic companies posing economic security risks for Japan that might benefit from government backing and boost profits in the long term.

item.title: Korea Plans Measures on Leveraged ETFs Driving Wild Volatility
item.description: South Korea will soon announce measures regarding the leveraged exchange-traded funds tied to shares of Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc. that have fueled a surge in market volatility.

item.title: IEA Boss Warns Global Economy in Peril If Hormuz Crisis Persists
item.description: The global economy faces a renewed challenge if the conflict that’s choked the Strait of Hormuz isn’t resolved in a matter of weeks, said International Energy Agency Executive Director Fatih Birol.

item.title: BHP Iron Ore Workers Stage First Port Hedland Strike Since 2000
item.description: Workers at BHP Group’s Port Hedland operations in Western Australia will stage the first strike at the company’s Pilbara iron ore hub since 2000, after last-ditch talks failed to avert industrial action.

item.title: Liquidity in Malaysia May Tighten Further as Rate-Hike Bets Grow
item.description: Funding conditions in Malaysia’s money market will likely tighten further later this year, with some analysts expecting stronger economic growth to prompt the country’s central bank to raise interest rates.

item.title: Yen Options Suggest a Slide to 165 Level Before Japan Intervenes
item.description: The yen has room to weaken more before Japanese officials step in to support the currency, options suggest.

item.title: Global Investors Hunt For Creative Backdoors Into China’s Mega CXMT IPO
item.description: Global investors largely shut out of China’s biggest IPO in nearly four years are looking at creative proxy trades as a way to profit from the country’s fast-rising memory-chip leader.

item.title: Iran War Drives New Investment in US LNG, S&P Global Says
item.description: The Iran war, and its disruptions across global energy markets, is spurring investments for new US liquefied natural gas export infrastructure, according to consulting firm S&P Global.

item.title: Li Ka-shing’s Cash-Out Plan Sets Up Empire for Leadership Shift
item.description: Billionaire Li Ka-shing and his family are preparing to usher in a new generation of leaders after some of their longest-serving lieutenants wrap up the sale of various assets to overhaul Hong Kong’s largest conglomerate.

item.title: Nvidia Expands Toyota AI Partnership for Smart Cities, Factories
item.description: Nvidia Corp. will supply its artificial intelligence hardware and software to Toyota Motor Corp. to power smart cities, traffic intelligence systems and carmaking factories, broadening a decade-long partnership that began with developing autonomous vehicles.

item.title: Gold Steadies as Soft Inflation, War Risk Cloud Fed Rate Outlook
item.description: Gold steadied, as traders weighed softer-than-expected inflation data against escalating attacks in the Middle East for clues to the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path.

item.title: BHP’s Iron Ore, Copper Output Slip as Miner Plans for Growth
item.description: BHP Group Ltd.’s iron ore production fell in the three months through June as the miner pushes ahead with expansions in copper and potash.

item.title: Data Center Firm Csquare Is Said to Price IPO at $21 Per Share
item.description: Csquare Inc. priced its initial public offering at $21 per share, according to people familiar with the matter, below a marketed range.

item.title: Oil Advances on Iran, Stocks Set for Mixed Open: Markets Wrap
item.description: Crude oil extended gains as the US launched fresh strikes on Iran, raising concerns that Middle East tensions will further disrupt energy supplies. Stocks in Asia are set to open mixed.
